sharedOpening.note: Scene 1 is a FIXED baked package and is NEVER planner-routed. The FS preflight measured it: 20/20 beats verbatim from public/starter-scenes.js, byte-identical across three independent launches, and zero provider calls to display it. So all arms share an identical opening and any downstream difference is attributable to what the reader did.
sharedOpening.howTheChoiceIsMade: The product mounts a two-button prompt (_mountSceneDecisionPrompt) built from the baked package's own axis. _advanceStagedScene REFUSES to request a continuation until the choice is recorded, and dispatches nothing while it is unrecorded — measured in the FS preflight. The corpus runner must therefore record the decision through the prompt's own handler, not by submitting say/do alone.

theRealAxis.axis: run in shame vs remain and see where Julian was taking it

a.label: run in shame
a.text: If she runs: the clearing lets her go, which is worse than being stopped; The Answer is still in her hand when she reaches the trees, and Julian has not followed.

b.label: remain and see where Julian was taking it
b.text: If she remains: she stays where the whole assembly can see her, holding The Answer, and lets Julian finish the question the Dohkar tried to end.

theRealAxis.provenance: _sceneDecisionAxis(), read from the running app at packet build time
theRealAxis.binary: EXACTLY TWO CHOICES EXIST. There is no third button, so no third axis choice is reachable. Arm C therefore shares arm B's axis choice and diverges in say/do only.

planRowWordingIsNotTheChoice.planRowSays: END ON THE DECISION: tear the gossamer band away and go to Seren, or hold the line she was told to hold.
planRowWordingIsNotTheChoice.correction: This is the Scene 1 plan row's own prose, and the FIRST version of this packet derived all three branches from it. It is NOT what the reader is asked. The product presents the axis above. Recorded here so the error is visible rather than overwritten.

A_run.label: run — run in shame
A_run.source: THE PRODUCT'S OWN AXIS, button A, read from _sceneDecisionAxis()
A_run.authoredConsequence: If she runs: the clearing lets her go, which is worse than being stopped; The Answer is still in her hand when she reaches the trees, and Julian has not followed.
A_run.action: I turn away from the clearing and walk, and I do not look at any of them.
A_run.dialogue: Nothing. I have nothing to say to any of you.

B_remain.label: remain — remain and see where Julian was taking it
B_remain.source: THE PRODUCT'S OWN AXIS, button B, read from _sceneDecisionAxis()
B_remain.authoredConsequence: If she remains: she stays where the whole assembly can see her, holding The Answer, and lets Julian finish the question the Dohkar tried to end.
B_remain.action: I stay where I am and keep my eyes on Julian, waiting to see what he does next.
B_remain.dialogue: I am still here. Say the rest of it.

C_remain_offscript.label: remain — remain and see where Julian was taking it, with words the axis does not anticipate
C_remain_offscript.source: SAME AXIS CHOICE AS ARM B. The axis offers only two buttons, so a third axis choice does not exist in the product. This arm diverges at the SAY/DO gate instead: the reader remains, and then names publicly what the scene left unsaid — a move the authored consequence for "remain" does not anticipate. It tests branch specificity under an identical recorded decision, which is a DIFFERENT question from H2's original one.
C_remain_offscript.action: I stay, and I say out loud what everyone in this clearing is pretending not to know.
C_remain_offscript.dialogue: Say whose wish it really was. Say it where they can all hear you.
